projects.name: Retail Analytics: Customer Segmentation & Revenue Optimization
projects.description: Analysis of retail transaction data to understand customer purchasing behavior, seasonal sales trends and product category performance, turned into recommendations for revenue, targeting and inventory planning.
highlights: 46–55 age group contributes the highest revenue; Saturdays generate maximum revenue.
Q4 recorded the highest sales while Q3 showed a seasonal dip.
Revenue differences driven by purchase volume, not pricing; medium baskets give the highest average transaction value.

projects.name: marginbridge
projects.description: A price-volume-mix margin bridge that reconciles exactly, plus price elasticity estimated with the discount confounder controlled, scored against synthetic data where the true elasticity is known.
highlights: Bridge on 6,231 transaction lines reconciles exactly: volume +341,470, mix −275,020, price −37,935.
Mix shift explains 88% of the margin headwind and price erosion 12%.
Corrected elasticity intervals cover the true value in every segment; naive estimates sit near zero.

projects.name: upliftpolicy
projects.description: Retention targeting by uplift instead of churn propensity, with Qini curves and doubly-robust policy evaluation that surfaces customers contact drives away.
highlights: Top 30% by uplift adds 4.47 points of retention; top 30% by churn score loses 0.23 points.
Sleeping dogs are 37% of the churn-ranked list vs 4% of the uplift-ranked list.
T-learner uplift correlates +0.638 with the true treatment effect; 34 tests.

projects.name: pacingloop
projects.description: Real-time campaign pacing with hour-of-week median/MAD baselines and a damped, rate-limited controller that avoids false alarms on normal seasonal peaks.
highlights: 4/4 planted incidents detected and classified with 0.00 false alarms per week.
Damped controller: 279 adjustments and 33 reversals vs 488 and 117 for a naive proportional controller.
MAD baseline moves only from 965 to 970 when incidents enter history, vs standard deviation 770 to 3465.

projects.name: consentgraph
projects.description: Identity resolution where per-purpose consent gates the graph join itself, with match quality measured as precision against planted ground truth and a household-confusion metric.
highlights: 1,432 source records resolved against 472 real people across 300 synthetic households.
Marketing purposes hold 1.0000 precision with zero household confusions.
Service purpose trades precision (0.8458) for 1.000 recall, reported rather than averaged.

projects.name: erasure
projects.description: GDPR erasure driven by column-level lineage across multiple data stores, verified by an adversary that tries to re-identify the person who was just deleted.
highlights: Lineage discovery finds 16 PII columns across 5 stores.
Naive table-list erasure leaves the subject identifiable; lineage-driven erasure does not.
Dry run by default, producing a certificate of tables touched and rows affected; 17 tests.

projects.name: dagcache
projects.description: A content-addressed, parallel pipeline runner for reproducible workflows that hashes code, params and data, explains why a stage is stale and traces artifact lineage.
highlights: SHA-256 cache keys over code, params and input content, with early cutoff to stop needless re-runs.
165 tests with mypy --strict and a coverage gate.
About 4,600 lines of typed Python with local or S3 remote caching.

projects.name: ratevault
projects.description: A motor insurance quote engine with bitemporal rate tables, so any past quote reprices exactly using the rates and rules in force at the time.
highlights: Backdated correction shows GBP 1995.19 as quoted vs GBP 1671.64 as corrected: GBP 323.55 owed back.
Factor-by-factor explanation of every premium; overlap protection enforced by database triggers.
Twelve tests run in CI on Node 24.

projects.name: permitflow
projects.description: A municipal permitting workflow where a declared statechart compiles to database constraints and triggers, so illegal status transitions are rejected by the database itself.
highlights: 11 states and 15 declared transitions compiled into a transition table and triggers.
Swept all 95 illegal pairs: 95 rejected, 0 accepted.
Append-only history; a raw-SQL bulk import that skips the application is rejected too.
